{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_25a111224c2046d69dfcc6d1","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Deliver a user's conversation list over the WebSocket protocol\n2\t\n3\tIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#144\n4\tLabels: type:feature, size:M, area:api, area:compliance, epic:extension-points\n5\t\n6\tPart of #35\n7\t\n8\t## Why\n9\t\n10\t#143 gives a consumer `store.listFor(userId)`.\n11\tIt does not give a **client** anything: the browser holding the socket cannot reach the store, so\n12\tevery consumer that wants a history sidebar has to stand up its own authenticated HTTP route over\n13\tthe same data the engine already authenticated on the upgrade. That is a second authorisation\n14\tpath to the same personal data, written once per consumer, each one able to get the ownership\n15\tcheck wrong in its own way — the exact failure #45 went out of its way to avoid for resume.\n16\t\n17\tA consumer may have no such route to extend: an engine deployment behind an api with a session\n18\tstore and no conversation endpoints of its own has nothing to add this to. The engine already knows who is connected and already\n19\treplays a conversation on resume; answering \"which conversations do I have\" over the same socket\n20\tis the smaller surface.\n21\t\n22\t## What to do\n23\t\n24\t- `src/types/messages.ts`, additive only:\n25\t  - `ListConversationsMessage {type: 'list_conversations'; limit?: number; before?: string}` into\n26\t    `IncomingMessage`. There is no user id field, and that is the point: the list is always the\n27\t    connection's authenticated user's.\n28\t  - `ConversationListMessage {type: 'conversation_list'; conversations: ConversationSummary[]}`\n29\t    into `OutgoingMessage`, where `ConversationSummary` is `SessionSummary` with its two times as\n30\t    ISO strings — `Date` does not survive `JSON.stringify` as a `Date`, and the protocol types\n31\t    describe what goes on the wire.\n32\t- `validation.ts`: a `list_conversations` case — `limit`, when present, an integer 1–200;\n33\t  `before`, when present, a string `Date.parse` accepts. Anything else is `INVALID_MESSAGE`, as\n34\t  the two existing cases do it.\n35\t- Handling: `createMessageHandler` takes the session store and the new options alongside the\n36\t  orchestrator (`createServer` already holds both), and answers `list_conversations` on the\n37\t  non-locked path beside `ping` — a history request is not a turn and must not queue behind a\n38\t  streaming answer.\n39\t- The user id comes from `ws.userId`, never from the frame. Add the regression:\n40\t  a frame carrying an extra `userId` of another user is answered with the connecting user's own\n41\t  list.\n42\t- Opt-in: `HalEngineConfig.transport.history?: {enabled: boolean}`, default off, threaded through\n43\t  `createServer`'s options like `resume`. With it off, `list_conversations` is answered with an\n44\t  `error` frame and no list.\n45\t- A store that implements no `listFor` is answered with an `error`, not an empty list: a client\n46\t  that renders \"no conversations\" for a user who has several is a worse answer than one that\n47\t  renders a failure. `ErrorCodes` gains one code for both cases (`UNSUPPORTED`), additive.\n48\t- Picking a conversation needs nothing new: the client reconnects with `?sessionId=<id>`, which\n49\t  #45 already ships with the ownership check and the replay. No in-band switch frame, no second\n50\t  replay path.\n51\t- Specs and docs: extend `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md` (the two frames, their\n52\t  field tables, the authorisation rule) and the conversation-list spec; add § Conversation list\n53\t  to `docs/getting-started.md` by editing `example/full-config.ts` and running `npm run docs:fix`\n54\t  — that listing sits under `<!-- doc-block: example/full-config.ts#full-config -->` and\n55\t  `npm run docs:check` fails a hand-edited block.\n56\t\n57\t## Decisions\n58\t\n59\t- **A frame, not a REST route.** The REST chat routes are demo-only and are not where a consumer is meant to build. The WebSocket is where the caller is\n60\t  already authenticated, once per connection, by the consumer's own `wsAuth`.\n61\t- **Its own opt-in flag, separate from `resume`.** Resume hands a client back a conversation it\n62\t  was already in; a list tells it what else the user has. A deployer who turned on resume did not\n63\t  thereby agree to the second disclosure, and a config that conflates them cannot be audited.\n64\t- **Answered off the per-session lock.** `PerSessionLock` serialises turns (#47). This was written before\n92\t      #143's review found that paging on a timestamp alone drops a conversation whenever two\n93\t      share an activity time, so the store's cursor became a composite that accepts an ISO\n94\t      string; a `Date` cannot carry the tie-break. no migration guide is owed\n- [ ] `npm run verify` passes and the coverage floors for the touched groups hold or rise\n\n## Amendments\n\nThree things changed between writing this issue and building it, each marked in the criterion it\naffects:\n\n1. **`before` is a cursor, not a timestamp.** #143's review found that paging on `updatedAt` alone\n   silently drops a conversation when two share an activity time. The store's cursor became\n   `{updatedAt, sessionId}`, so the frame carries both halves and the validator refuses one half\n   alone. Built as originally written, the transport would have reintroduced the defect the store\n   had just been fixed for.\n2. **`messages.ts` gains four interfaces, not two** — the two frames plus the two payload types\n   they describe.\n3. **`StoreCannotList` is new public surface**, beyond what this issue specified: without it a\n   permanent store misconfiguration cannot be told from a transient failure, in either the client\n   frame or the log.\n\nTwo decisions the criteria did not anticipate:\n\n- **`transport.history` without `transport.resume` is useless, and now says so.** `?sessionId=` is\n  read only when resume is enabled, so a list whose rows cannot be opened is a deployment slip:\n  the engine warns at startup and the documentation says so where it tells a client to reconnect\n  with a row's id. Refusing to start was considered and rejected as too blunt for a library.\n- **The conversation the connection is in is listed like any other**, so a fresh connect sees a row\n  of its own holding no entries. Filtering it out was rejected: it is a real conversation the user\n  is in, and it is their newest the moment they send anything.\n\n## Tech notes\n\nDepends on #143: without `listFor` there is\nnothing to send.\n\nKey paths: `src/types/messages.ts`, `src/types/session.ts` (`ErrorCodes`),\n`src/transport/ws/{validation,messageHandler,sender}.ts`, `src/transport/createServer.ts`,\n`src/config.ts`, `example/full-config.ts`, `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md`.\n\nOut of scope: a preview or title on the summaries (its own issue); deleting a conversation from\nthe client, which would put an erasure primitive on the wire and needs its own authorisation\ndecision; paging state held server-side — the client pages with `before`; an operator view of\nanother user's conversations, which is an authorisation question of its own; and live sync between open tabs,\nwhich #124 ruled out.\n\nRefs #143, #145, #41, #45, #47, #124\n\n\n\n\n","numLines":174,"startLine":1,"totalLines":174}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_25a111224c2046d69dfcc6d1","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

The client on the other end of the WebSocket has no way to ask for it, and the consumer who wants a conversation picker without standing up their own REST endpoint has to write one anyway.\n\n**Strategy: `direct`** — `createServer` and the WebSocket upgrade/message pipeline already exist and accept frames over a real WebSocket connection, so acceptance tests can connect today, send `list_sessions` frames, and fail directly on the missing `session_list` and `list_sessions` validation/dispatch behaviour.\n\n## Done when these pass\n\n- [ ] **listing conversations over the WebSocket protocol › answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId** — Sends `{type: 'list_sessions', limit, before, userId}` over a connected WebSocket and verifies `store.listFor` is called with the socket's authenticated `userId` (`session.userId`) and `{limit, before}`, answering `{type: 'session_list', sessions}` with `createdAt` and `updatedAt` serialised as ISO-8601 strings.\n  `src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts`\n\n- [ ] **listing conversations over the WebSocket protocol › answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws** — Verifies that a store without `listFor` answers `{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}` and a store whose `listFor` throws/rejects logs an error under category `'ws'` with the userId and error message and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}`.\n  `src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts`\n\n- [ ] **listing conversations over the WebSocket protocol › accepts a bare list_sessions frame and rejects a malformed limit or before with INVALID_MESSAGE without calling listFor** — Verifies that `{type: 'list_sessions'}` is accepted while non-integer or negative `limit` values and malformed `before` cursors (`sessionId` outside 1–128 chars or unparseable `updatedAt`) are rejected with `INVALID_MESSAGE` without invoking `store.listFor`.\n  `src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts`\n\n## Facets\n\n- [ ] Add `ListSessionsMessage`, `SessionSummaryFrame`, and `SessionListMessage` to `src/types/messages.ts`, include them in `IncomingMessage` and `OutgoingMessage`, and re-export them from `src/index.ts`.\n- [ ] Validate `list_sessions` frames in `src/transport/ws/validation.ts` (optional non-negative integer `limit`; optional `before` object with 1–128 char `sessionId` and finite-date `updatedAt` string or number; strip unknown fields like `userId`).\n- [ ] Thread `sessionStore` into `createMessageHandler` (optional parameter so existing 1-arg and 2-arg callers keep working) and wire it in `src/transport/createServer.ts`.\n- [ ] Handle `list_sessions` in `src/transport/ws/messageHandler.ts` (and helper in `src/transport/ws/sender.ts` if needed) by reading `session.userId`, calling `await sessionStore?.listFor?.(session.userId, {limit, before})`, serialising `Date` fields to ISO strings, and on error logging via `log.error('ws', ...)` and sending `ErrorCodes.SERVER_ERROR`.\n- [ ] Document `list_sessions` and `session_list` in `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md` and `specs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md`.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Conversation titles or previews (first user message, model-generated title).\n- Deleting or renaming a conversation from the client over the socket.\n- Switching the socket's active session in place (`?sessionId=` on reconnect is how a conversation is rejoined).\n- Holding pagination cursor state server-side (the client pages with `before`).\n- An operator view of another user's conversations or live sync between open {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_a33ba20fcb994bb8945f9d42","type":"tool_result","content":"hal-engine-abandon-on-close\nhal-engine-architecture\nhal-engine-awaitable-session-store\nhal-engine-before-tool-call-hook\nhal-engine-chat-routes\nhal-engine-commit-open-entries\nhal-engine-config-hooks\nhal-engine-conversation-list\nhal-engine-doc-gates\nhal-engine-mongo-session-store\nhal-engine-npm-release\nhal-engine-providers\nhal-engine-session-lifetime\nhal-engine-session-resume\nhal-engine-session-write-signal\nhal-engine-single-terminal-frame\nhal-engine-spec-anchor-drift\nhal-engine-spec-link-placement\nhal-engine-spec-status\nhal-engine-subprotocol-marker\nhal-engine-thinking-tag-parser\nhal-engine-tool-budget\nhal-engine-tool-executor-throw\nhal-engine-tool-input-validation\nhal-engine-tool-responses\nhal-engine-websocket-protocol\n# Conversation List\n\n| Field  | Value                 |\n| ------ | --------------------- |\n| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#143 |\n| Status | Shipped               |\n\nResume gets a client back into one conversation: the id it names, or the user's most recently active one. Neither tells it which conversations exist, and every other member of `SessionStore` answers about a session the caller can already name, so a consumer wanting to offer a conversation list had to query the collection behind the engine's back, against a document shape and a key the engine owns. `listFor` answers the list instead, as summaries rather than sessions. **GDPR.** A summary is personal data — that a user held a conversation, and when — so it carries no conversation content, it is filtered to one user by the query rather than in application code afterwards, and the retention bound stays the consumer's, through the store's `maxAgeMs` and erasure methods and re-cinq/HALEngine#41.\n\n## The summary\n\n- A summary is `sessionId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and `entryCount`, and nothing else: neither the conversation's entries nor its credentials, so a list can never hand over either, even for a session created with credentials ([validated by: carries only its four fields, so a list can never hand over a conversation or a credential](../../src/infrastructure/stores/sessionStoreListSignature.test.ts#L22)).\n- `listFor` is optional, like `latestFor` and `lookup` before it: a store written against the five original members still satisfies the interface, and both shipped stores implement it ([validated by: leaves a store with only the five original members satisfying the interface beside both shipped ones](../../src/infrastructure/stores/sessionStoreListSignature.test.ts#L11)).\n\n## The order a list answers in\n\n- Summaries come back most recent activity first ([validated by: answers newest activity first, headed by the very session latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L27)).\n- The first summary is the session `latestFor` returns, because both read the same activity ([validated by: answers newest activity first, headed by the very session latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L27)).\n- The order is total rather than merely sorted: two conversations last active in the same millisecond are ordered by session id, the larger first, which is what lets a page resume without dropping one of them ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on activity rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L141)).\n- In `InMemorySessionStore` that tie-break is the list's alone: `latestFor` breaks the same tie by creation order, so for two tied conversations the head of the list and the session a resume rejoins can differ ([validated by: breaks a tie on activity by session id, where latestFor takes the session created later](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L42)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` answers in order of `updatedAt`, which each `save` moves forward, and its first summary is the session its own `latestFor` returns ([validated by: answers the user's conversations newest saved first, headed by the one latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L31)).\n- It breaks a tie by `_id` in both members, so there the head of the list is the session a resume rejoins even when every conversation shares an `updatedAt` ([validated by: heads the list with the session latestFor returns even when every conversation shares an updatedAt](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L161)).\n\n## What a summary reports\n\n- `InMemorySessionStore` reports the moment `create` was called, the newest entry time as the activity, and the conversation's entry count ([validated by: reports a creation time, the newest activity and the entry count of each conversation](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L53)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` reports the document's `createdAt`, the `updatedAt` its last save wrote, and the counter written beside the entries ([validated by: reports the creation time, the last save and the entry count of each conversation](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L49)).\n- That counter is what a save writes, so a list never reads a conversation to count one ([validated by: counts a conversation from the field a save writes beside the entries](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L95)).\n- A document written before the counter existed reads as a conversation of no entries rather than failing the list, which is what the backlog documented in `docs/session-stores.md` is for ([validated by: reads a conversation saved before the counter existed as one of no entries, rather than failing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L79)).\n\n## Whose conversations\n\n- A list holds only the asking user's conversations: another user's never appear, and a user with none gets an empty list ([validated by: omits a conversation that aged out and another user's, and answers nothing for a user with none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L65)).\n- `InMemorySessionStore` omits a conversation that has aged out, as `latestFor` does ([validated by: omits a conversation that aged out and another user's, and answers nothing for a user with none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L65)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` filters on the user in the database, sorts on `{updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}` — the `{userId: 1, updatedAt: -1}` index `latestFor` already needs serves its leading keys — and asks for a projection that leaves the entries behind ([validated by: asks the database to filter on the user, sort on the index with the id behind it, and never for the entries](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L108)).\n- It answers from that projection alone, so a collection that never returns an entry still lists conversations — the conversation does not leave the database to be listed ([validated by: answers from a projection alone, so a collection that never returns entries still lists conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L181)).\n\n## Paging\n\n- `limit` takes that many of the newest, and `before` resumes after a row, so a client pages by passing back the last summary it saw — `SessionCursor` is `updatedAt` and `sessionId`, which a `SessionSummary` already satisfies ([validated by: pages down the same order: a limit takes the newest, and before takes what is older than it](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L78)).\n- Paging walks every conversation exactly once even when all of them share an activity time, because the cursor carries the session id the order breaks ties on: a tie cannot fall between two pages and be skipped ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on activity rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L141)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` pages the same way ([validated by: pages with before and a limit, down the same newest-first order](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L62)).\n- It walks a tie exactly once too, through the same cursor ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on updatedAt rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L127)).\n- A list is at most 200 summaries however many are asked for, and 50 when none is asked for, so no caller can ask for an unbounded page ([validated by: answers at most two hundred conversations however many are asked for, and fifty when none is](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L94)).\n- That limit bounds the rows answered, not the rows the database reads to answer them: on `MongoSessionStore` the work is bounded by the `{userId: 1, updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}` index `docs/session-stores.md` prescribes, and under the two-key form Mongo sorts the user's whole history before applying the limit ([validated by: needs the three-key index to answer without sorting the whole history, which the two-key form does not](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L192)).\n- A fractional limit is floored rather than refused, since a slip in a limit is not a reason to deny a user their history ([validated by: floors a fractional limit, and reads a negative or unusable one as none given rather than as nothing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L104)).\n- A negative limit, and one that is not a usable number, are read as no limit given at all rather than as a limit of none: handing a user an empty history for a typo is the worse reading ([validated by: floors a fractional limit, and reads a negative or unusable one as none given rather than as nothing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L104)).\n- Only a limit of exactly `0` answers no conversations ([validated by: answers nothing only for a limit of exactly none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L116)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` answers a limit of `0` without querying, because MongoDB reads `limit: 0` as no limit at all and would otherwise answer with every conversation the filter matches ([validated by: answers a limit of none without asking the database, which reads a limit of zero as no limit at all](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L143)).\n\n## The two shipped stores answer one order\n\n- `InMemorySessionStore` and `MongoSessionStore` list the same conversations in the same order, so a consumer swapping one for the other sees the same conversation list ([validated by: answer the same order for conversations whose activity differs](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L43)).\n- They break a tie on activity the same way, by session id ([validated by: break a tie on activity the same way, by session id](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L52)).\n- They page identically through the documented call, `listFor(userId, {limit, before: rows.at(-1)})`, a page at a time until a page comes back empty ([validated by: page the same way through the documented call, two rows at a time from the last row seen](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L61)).\n\n## A cursor the caller can actually hold\n\n- A cursor's `updatedAt` may be a `Date`, an ISO string or an epoch number, so a summary that went through JSON on its way to a client and back still pages ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, and refuses one carrying no usable moment](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L123)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` reads such a cursor as a date before it queries, since a string compares against no stored BSON date and would quietly match none of them ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, where a string would have matched no stored date](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L150)).\n- A cursor carrying no usable moment is refused with an error naming it, rather than read as no cursor at all, which would answer the first page again and repeat rows a client has already shown ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, and refuses one carrying no usable moment](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L123)).\n\n## A collection that cannot list\n\n- `find` is optional on `CollectionLike`, so an adapter written before conversation lists existed still satisfies the port ([validated by: refuses to list on a collection that implements no find, rather than reporting no conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L175)).\n- A store built on a collection without it refuses to list, rather than reporting that the user has no conversations ([validated by: refuses to list on a collection that implements no find, rather than reporting no conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L175)).\n\n## When the store cannot answer\n\n- A store whose collection fails rejects rather than answering a partial or empty list: what to show a user who may have conversations is the caller's decision, and an empty history is not a safe guess ([validated by: rejects rather than answering a partial list when the collection fails](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L225)).\n\n## Over the WebSocket protocol\n\n- A client sends `{type: 'list_sessions', limit?, before?}` and receives `{type: 'session_list', sessions}` for the socket's authenticated user, with `createdAt` and `updatedAt` serialised as ISO-8601 strings and any client-supplied `userId` ignored ([validated by: answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L87)).\n- A store without `listFor` answers `{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}`, and a throwing `listFor` logs an error on the `ws` category and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}` ([validated by: answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L129)).\n- The validator accepts an optional non-negative integer `limit` and an optional `before` cursor whose `sessionId` is 1–128 characters and whose `updatedAt` parses as a valid timestamp, rejecting any other `list_sessions` payload with `INVALID_MESSAGE` without calling `listFor` ([validated by: accepts a bare list_sessions frame and rejects a malformed limit or before with INVALID_MESSAGE without calling listFor](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L161)).","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a4c5379c-fbcf-40b2-a051-dad8c7dba5d6","uuid":"984c859e-1a25-4f6e-9749-ab51757eb2be","timestamp":"2026-10-31T18:40:15.310Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"hal-engine-abandon-on-close\nhal-engine-architecture\nhal-engine-awaitable-session-store\nhal-engine-before-tool-call-hook\nhal-engine-chat-routes\nhal-engine-commit-open-entries\nhal-engine-config-hooks\nhal-engine-conversation-list\nhal-engine-doc-gates\nhal-engine-mongo-session-store\nhal-engine-npm-release\nhal-engine-providers\nhal-engine-session-lifetime\nhal-engine-session-resume\nhal-engine-session-write-signal\nhal-engine-single-terminal-frame\nhal-engine-spec-anchor-drift\nhal-engine-spec-link-placement\nhal-engine-spec-status\nhal-engine-subprotocol-marker\nhal-engine-thinking-tag-parser\nhal-engine-tool-budget\nhal-engine-tool-executor-throw\nhal-engine-tool-input-validation\nhal-engine-tool-responses\nhal-engine-websocket-protocol\n# newest, and before takes what is older than it](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L78)).\n- Paging walks every conversation exactly once even when all of them share an activity time, because the cursor carries the session id the order breaks ties on: a tie cannot fall between two pages and be skipped ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on activity rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L141)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` pages the same way ([validated by: pages with before and a limit, down the same newest-first order](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L62)).\n- It walks a tie exactly once too, through the same cursor ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on updatedAt rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L127)).\n- A list is at most 200 summaries however many are asked for, and 50 when none is asked for, so no caller can ask for an unbounded page ([validated by: answers at most two hundred conversations however many are asked for, and fifty when none is](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L94)).\n- That limit bounds the rows answered, not the rows the database reads to answer them: on `MongoSessionStore` the work is bounded by the `{userId: 1, updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}` index `docs/session-stores.md` prescribes, and under the two-key form Mongo sorts the user's whole history before applying the limit ([validated by: needs the three-key index to answer without sorting the whole history, which the two-key form does not](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L192)).\n- A fractional limit is floored rather than refused, since a slip in a limit is not a reason to deny a user their history ([validated by: floors a fractional limit, and reads a negative or unusable one as none given rather than as nothing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L104)).\n- A negative limit, and one that is not a usable number, are read as no limit given at all rather than as a limit of none: handing a user an empty history for a typo is the worse reading ([validated by: floors a fractional limit, and reads a negative or unusable one as none given rather than as nothing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L104)).\n- Only a limit of exactly `0` answers no conversations ([validated by: answers nothing only for a limit of exactly none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L116)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` answers a limit of `0` without querying, because MongoDB reads `limit: 0` as no limit at all and would otherwise answer with every conversation the filter matches ([validated by: answers a limit of none without asking the database, which reads a limit of zero as no limit at all](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L143)).\n\n## The two shipped stores answer one order\n\n- `InMemorySessionStore` and `MongoSessionStore` list the same conversations in the same order, so a consumer swapping one for the other sees the same conversation list ([validated by: answer the same order for conversations whose activity differs](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L43)).\n- They break a tie on activity the same way, by session id ([validated by: break a tie on activity the same way, by session id](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L52)).\n- They page identically through the documented call, `listFor(userId, {limit, before: rows.at(-1)})`, a page at a time until a page comes back empty ([validated by: page the same way through the documented call, two rows at a time from the last row seen](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L61)).\n\n## A cursor the caller can actually hold\n\n- A cursor's `updatedAt` may be a `Date`, an ISO string or an epoch number, so a summary that went through JSON on its way to a client and back still pages ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, and refuses one carrying no usable moment](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L123)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` reads such a cursor as a date before it queries, since a string compares against no stored BSON date and would quietly match none of them ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, where a string would have matched no stored date](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L150)).\n- A cursor carrying no usable moment is refused with an error naming it, rather than read as no cursor at all, which would answer the first page again and repeat rows a client has already shown ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, and refuses one carrying no usable moment](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L123)).\n\n## A collection that cannot list\n\n- `find` is optional on `CollectionLike`, so an adapter written before conversation lists existed still satisfies the port ([validated by: refuses to list on a collection that implements no find, rather than reporting no conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L175)).\n- A store built on a collection without it refuses to list, rather than reporting that the user has no conversations ([validated by: refuses to list on a collection that implements no find, rather than reporting no conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L175)).\n\n## When the store cannot answer\n\n- A store whose collection fails rejects rather than answering a partial or empty list: what to show a user who may have conversations is the caller's decision, and an empty history is not a safe guess ([validated by: rejects rather than answering a partial list when the collection fails](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L225)).\n\n## Over the WebSocket protocol\n\n- A client sends `{type: 'list_sessions', limit?, before?}` and receives `{type: 'session_list', sessions}` for the socket's authenticated user, with `createdAt` and `updatedAt` serialised as ISO-8601 strings and any client-supplied `userId` ignored ([validated by: answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L87)).\n- A store without `listFor` answers `{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}`, and a throwing `listFor` logs an error on the `ws` category and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}` ([validated by: answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L129)).\n- The validator accepts an optional non-negative integer `limit` and an optional `before` cursor whose `sessionId` is 1–128 characters and whose `updatedAt` parses as a valid timestamp, rejecting any other `list_sessions` payload with `INVALID_MESSAGE` without calling `listFor` ([validated by: accepts a bare list_sessions frame and rejects a malformed limit or before with INVALID_MESSAGE without calling listFor](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L161)).","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_a33ba20fcb994bb8945f9d42","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{\n      spec: doc('specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md').includes(\n        `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: ${HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL}, <access-token>`\n      ),\n      client: doc('docs/getting-started.md').includes(`['${HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL}', token]`),\n    };\n\n    expect({marker: HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL, printed}).toEqual({marker: 'hal.v1', printed: {spec: true, client: true}});\n  });\n});\n\ndescribe('selectSubprotocol', () => {\n  it('answers the marker when it is offered first, never the token beside it', () => {\n    expect(selectSubprotocol(new Set([HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL, TOKEN]))).toBe(HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL);\n  });\n\n  it('answers the marker when it is offered after the token', () => {\n    expect(selectSubprotocol(new Set([TOKEN, HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL]))).toBe(HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL);\n  });\n\n  it('answers nothing for a bare token offered without the marker', () => {\n    expect(selectSubprotocol(new Set([TOKEN]))).toBe(false);\n  });\n\n  it('answers nothing for an empty offer', () => {\n    expect(selectSubprotocol(new Set())).toBe(false);\n  });\n});\n\ndescribe('credentialFromSubprotocol', () => {\n  it('reads the token from a marker-first offer', () => {\n    expect(credentialFromSubprotocol(`${HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL}, ${TOKEN}`)).toBe(TOKEN);\n  });\n\n  it('reads the token from a token-first offer', () => {\n expect(credentialFromSubprotocol(`${HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL}, first, second`)).toBe('first');\n  });\n\n  it('reads nothing from a bare token offered without the marker', () => {\n    expect(credentialFromSubprotocol(TOKEN)).toBeUndefined();\n  });\n\n  it('reads nothing when only the marker is offered', () => {\n    expect(credentialFromSubprotocol(HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL)).toBeUndefined();\n  });\n\n\n=====LORE LIST=====\n#!/usr/bin/env node\n// Emits the Lore test-command `list` shape: a single JSON array of\n// process from 'node:process';\n\nconst reportFile = join(tmpdir(), `hal-engine-jest-report-${process.pid}.json`);\n\ntry {\n  execFileSync('npx', ['jest', '--json', `--outputFile=${reportFile}`], {\n    cwd: process.cwd(),\n    stdio: ['ignore', 'ignore', 'inherit'],\n    // The suite runs as ESM; jest needs the flag in every spawn, not just npm test.\n    env: {...process.env, NODE_OPTIONS: `${process.env.NODE_OPTIONS ?? ''} --experimental-vm-modules`.trim()},\n  });\n} catch {\n  // A failing test still produces a full report, and listing must not depend\n  // on the suite being green. An unreadable report below is the real failure.\n}\n\nlet report;\n\ntry {\n  report = JSON.parse(readFileSync(reportFile, 'utf8'));\n} catch (error) {\n  process.stderr.write(`jest produced no readable report at ${reportFile}: ${error.message}\\n`);\n  process.exit(1);\n} finally {\n  rmSync(reportFile, {force: true});\n}\n\nconst tests = report.testResults.flatMap(suite => {\n  const file = relative(process.cwd(), suite.name);\n\n  return suite.assertionResults.map(assertion => ({\n    id: `${file}::${assertion.fullName}`,\n    name: assertion.fullName,\n    file,\n  }));\n});\n\nprocess.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify(tests)}\\n`);","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a4c5379c-fbcf-40b2-a051-dad8c7dba5d6","uuid":"600afb34-fc7c-4784-b431-76e30c525b2a","timestamp":"2026-10-31T18:41:27.596Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"import 1 : -1;\n}\n\n/** The cursor's moment, from a `Date`, an ISO string or an epoch number, so a row that went through JSON still pages. */\nexport function cursorAt(cursor: SessionCursor): number {\n  const time = new Date(cursor.updatedAt).getTime();\n  // Loudly, because every silent reading is wrong: page one again duplicates rows, and no page at all hides history.\n  if (!Number.isFinite(time)) throw new Error(`listFor cursor has no usable updatedAt: ${String(cursor.updatedAt)}`);\n  return time;\n}\n\n/** Whether a summary sits after the cursor in that order, which is what keeps a tie from falling between two pages. */\nexport function sitsAfter(summary: SessionSummary, cursorTime: number, cursorId: string): boolean {\n  const gap = summary.updatedAt.getTime() - cursorTime;\n  return gap < 0 || (gap === 0 && summary.sessionId < cursorId);\n}\n\n=====STATUS CHECK=====\n// Local counterpart of the ADR half of require-status-matches-coverage:\n// an ADR must declare a lifecycle status the parsers can read, while staying\n// exempt from the coverage tier that rule would also demand of it. docArgs.map((path) => relative(root, resolve(root, path))) : discoverDocs();\n\nconst readDoc = (docPath) => {\n  try {\n    return readFileSync(join(root, docPath), \"utf8\");\n  } catch (error) {\n    process.stderr.write(`cannot read doc ${docPath}: ${error.message}\\n`);\n    process.exit(2);","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_24199a863dbd436c94a0bacf","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}
